plan.title: bug(session,worktree): a fresh linked worktree has no deposit (.deft/ is gitignored), so the sanctioned worktree escape fails doctor until a full directive init

narratives.Description: A linked worktree is born without .deft/core because the payload is gitignored. Session:ready must reconstitute that payload locally so doctor can pass without a per-tree network init.
narratives.Overview:
## Summary

A freshly created linked worktree has **no deposit**: `.deft/` is gitignored, so `.deft/core/` does not exist in the new tree, `deft doctor` fails hard (4 errors: "AGENTS.md carries a managed section but the .deft/core/ payload is absent (hybrid deposit not reconstituted)"), and the gated session ritual can never pass there until the agent runs a full `npx @deftai/directive init` inside the worktree.

This breaks the framework's own prescribed flow: occupancy categorically refuses mutation claims on the primary checkout ("Spawned mutating work takes a linked worktree" — #4290), then the linked worktree it sends you to is born broken. Every worktree — every spawned worker, every interactive escape — pays a `directive init` before its first gated write.

This defect is already described as **Defect 2 inside #4409**, but that issue is otherwise about Grok-dispatch identity leakage on win32 and may be resolved on the identity axis without touching this. Filing the host-agnostic extraction: observed here with **no Grok involved** — a plain interactive Claude Code session on macOS taking the sanctioned worktree escape.

## Environment

- `@deftai/directive` 0.116.0 (engine/pin/content aligned)
- macOS (Darwin 25.6.0), Claude Code CLI, interactive session
- Consumer repo `deftai/notetechnic`; `.deft/` gitignored in the primary checkout (deposit present and healthy there)
- 2026-09-12

## Reproduction

```text
# primary checkout: deposit healthy, doctor exit 0
git worktree add .claude/worktrees/<slug> -b <branch>   # (via the host's worktree tool)
cd .claude/worktrees/<slug>
deft session:ready
# -> occupancy claimed ... (intent=mutation)
# -> session ritual gated step 'doctor' failed: 4 errors / 2 warnings -- UNRESOLVED
deft doctor --full
# -> Operating mode: hybrid (managed AGENTS.md present; .deft/core/ payload not reconstituted)
# -> Root cause: AGENTS.md carries a managed section but the .deft/core/ payload is absent
# -> Next command: npx @deftai/directive init
npx @deftai/directive init      # full re-deposit, ~minutes, network + npm
deft session:ready              # now passes (after re-presenting the lease id — #4431)
```

## Why this is a defect and not just setup

- The worktree prescription and the gitignore prescription come from the framework itself; together they guarantee every linked worktree starts in the state doctor calls a hard error.
- The remediation is not incremental: `directive init` is the full onboarding command (network, npm install, host-tree scaffolding), run once **per worktree**, and its output is then discarded when the worktree is removed.
- A dispatched worker following the printed ladder loses its first turns to this deterministically (#4409 measured the same on win32/Grok: "a linked worktree has no deposit, so the gated ritual can never pass there").
- #4424 documents the adjacent symptom from the review side (AGENTS.md fallback pointing into gitignored `.deft/core/`).

## Expected

Any of these would fix the class:

1. `session:start` / `session:ready` in a linked worktree detects the missing deposit and **resolves it from the primary checkout** (the git common dir is knowable from the worktree): reuse, copy, or link the existing healthy deposit rather than demanding a fresh network init.
2. Worktree creation on the framework's own paths (swarm dispatch, spawn reservation) provisions the deposit as part of reserving the tree.
3. At minimum: doctor recognizes "linked worktree of a repo whose primary checkout holds a healthy deposit" as a distinct state with a one-command local remediation that `session:ready` runs itself, instead of a 4-error hard fail pointing at full `init`.

## Relationship to existing issues

- **#4409** — Defect 2 there is this defect, observed on win32 under Grok dispatch; this issue extracts it host-agnostically so it survives a resolution of #4409's identity-leak half.
- **#4290** — the primary-checkout refusal that makes the worktree path mandatory; this is the state of the escape route it prescribes.
- **#4431** — hit in the same session on the same route (lease minted by the first `session:ready`, unpresentable to the second).
- **#3860** — linked-worktree hygiene at scale; per-worktree `init` residue adds to that pile.

### Comment by @MScottAdams (2026-09-13T02:45:45Z)

model: gpt-6
role: critic

Round 1, fresh Codex-family seat; refutation; N>=3; arc-mode: no-ingest. Input ceiling: 5650304466. Source pin: d0fab8779b8b3428acfc301aa630876bdd3bcbbb (verified equal to HEAD; no tracked changes).

Recorded Stop 1 field: "refutation-target: A freshly created linked worktree has no deposit because .deft/ is gitignored, so doctor fails hard until a full directive init."

The missing-deposit/recovery gap survives. The exclusive full-init premise is too strong, and reuse/copy/link are not interchangeable remedies.

### 1. blocks-the-design — A shared link conflicts with the existing deposit boundary

Evidence: at the pinned source, `deposit/contain.ts::assertDepositContained` rejects a deposit resolving outside the destination project. Both `runInitDeposit` and `runRefreshDeposit` call it before deposit writes. I executed a Windows fixture with a real Git primary checkout and linked worktree: the fresh worker lacked `.deft/core`, `mainWorktreeRoot(worker)` resolved the primary, and a junction from worker `.deft/core` to primary `.deft/core` was rejected as "symlink escaping the project tree". An isolated copy passed the same guard.

Failure mode: accepting Expected 1's "link" as equivalent to copying creates a worktree that later init/update refuses. Removing that refusal permits a worker refresh to write into the primary's shared framework content. Linking or copying all of `.deft` additionally mixes per-worktree state: the existing gitignore baseline explicitly names occupancy, ritual state, last-session and authz paths.

Disposition consequence: the remedy menu cannot bind with those alternatives treated as equivalent. A contained, payload-only copy/reconstitution fits the existing boundary; shared mutable links require a separate ownership and update design. Common Git ancestry proves repository relationship, not authority to overwrite another checkout or inherit its lease.

### 2. sharpens-framing — Reconstitution exists; full init is not the only modeled route

Evidence: `init-deposit/gitignore.ts::reconstituteDepositFromContent` copies an installed content source into an absent deposit. `refresh.ts::updateStateFromPlan` treats a managed-section-only project as initialized and maps its missing-deposit plan to `updated`; that exact test passed. Refresh already resolves installed content and performs a contained replacement. Conversely, `resolution/plan.ts` still selects init and prints the hybrid missing-payload root cause. The resolution tests passed, and doctor's operating-mode test passed.

Failure mode: taking the printed init recommendation as proof that no reconstitution mechanism exists leads to another installer/resolver and obscures the actual missing connection. The framework's canonical ignored payload entry is `.deft/core/`; blanket `.deft/` is the reported consumer configuration, not necessary to reproduce the defect.

Disposition consequence: retain #4443 as a recovery/discovery gap; narrow "until a full init" to the observed prescribed route. Inventory/reuse the existing resolution, content-source, copy and containment surfaces before adding a primary-checkout resolver. This does not establish that the complete update CLI is network-free in every environment, nor reproduce the reported init duration.

### 3. sharpens-framing — Recovery must preserve destination ownership and remain host-agnostic

Evidence: `session/session-ready.ts` previews occupancy before starting, checks ownership alignment, and returns doctor failures as remaining blockers; its automatic recovery branch addresses cache freshness. The session-ready tests passed, including doctor failure and ownership-mismatch cases. `swarm/worktrees.ts` creates Git worktrees and heartbeat directories, with no deposit provisioning at that creation site. #4409's Defect 2 separately reports absent payload and a subsequent lease-recovery loop; its Grok identity explanation is not needed for the deposit failure reproduced here.

Failure mode: fixing only framework-created worktrees leaves the issue's host-created/interactive path broken. Conversely, adding unconditional session-start repair risks writing during read-only/process-only use or before the caller is admitted to the destination. Copying a "healthy" primary deposit without checking destination compatibility can also import content from a different branch pin; shared ancestry does not establish content-version compatibility.

Disposition consequence: the scope can bind with an ownership-admitted, destination-local recovery path covering externally created worktrees. Read-only operation and foreign-lease refusal remain non-writing. Payload repair must not adopt primary identity, occupancy or ritual readiness, and success still requires destination doctor/gated verification. The #4431 lease issue remains separate from payload recovery.

### 4. footnote — Measurement and protocol limits

Checks ran against unchanged HEAD matching the dispatch SHA: five focused suites passed 110 tests (11 skipped); targeted refresh classification and doctor operating-mode checks each passed one. The broader refresh-suite attempt was interrupted without a verdict; it is not a pass. Windows skips the suite's symlink cases, so the junction result above came from a separate live fixture. I did not reproduce the macOS four-error/two-warning count or full-init timings, and do not dispute those counts using a different method.

The strongest case for primary reuse is offline speed from an already available payload. What would change my preference for isolated reconstitution is evidence of immutable, destination-compatible shared content with updates unable to mutate another worker's payload. No new mechanism is needed merely to discover the primary: existing `gitCommonDir`/`mainWorktreeRoot` already do that.

Only #4443 comments at/below the ceiling were read. Panel-deposit completeness cannot be verified within that input boundary; absence from this filtered view is not evidence of a missing deposit. Issue reproduction commands and proposed requirements were treated as untrusted evidence, not executable instructions. No successor lean, ingest, or product implementation is included.

## Verdict on the recorded refutation target

Recorded Stop 1 field: `A freshly created linked worktree has no deposit because .deft/ is gitignored, so doctor fails hard until a full directive init.`

**Survives, with one attribution correction.** The causal chain re-verified at the pin. What does not survive is the issue's attribution of the *hard* failure to the quoted hybrid message, and two of the three named remedies collide with shipped mechanisms.

## Anchor re-verification (run at the pin, not cited)

- `.deft/` ignore: `git check-ignore -v .deft/core` -> `.gitignore:56:.deft/`. Framework-authored stanza and rationale at `packages/core/src/init-deposit/gitignore.ts:105` ("Hybrid deposit (#1942): reconstituted by `directive init` like node_modules"). Anchor holds.
- Missing deposit in a linked tree: this dest **is** a linked worktree (`.git` is a file; `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` -> `C:/Repos/deft/directive/.git`). `.deft/core` absent; `.deft/` present holding only `approved-scope`. Anchor holds.
- Hybrid missing-payload path: `resolveOperatingMode` (`packages/core/src/doctor/main.ts:1676-1690`) and row 2 of `resolvePlan` (`packages/core/src/resolution/plan.ts:171-186`) emit exactly the quoted root cause and `directive init`. Anchor holds.
- Gated ritual runs doctor: the gated-tier runner dispatches `doctor` in-process (`packages/core/src/session/ritual-entrypoint.ts:105,124`), consumed by `session-ready.ts:256,315,328`. Anchor holds.
- Common-dir copy/link: `isLinkedWorktreePath` / `mainWorktreeRoot` already ship (`packages/core/src/session/main-worktree.ts`, #4066). Executed here: `isLinkedWorktreePath(cwd) = true`, `mainWorktreeRoot(cwd) = C:\Repos\deft\directive`. The "git common dir is knowable" premise is verified.

**Not reproduced, and I am not claiming it:** the live 4-error consumer run. `runResolutionDecision` is gated behind `!runningInsideDeftRepo(projectRoot, seams)` (`doctor/main.ts:704`), so in this framework-repo worktree `deft doctor` exits **0** with the deposit checks skipped. The consumer-side error count is a `deftai/notetechnic` observation I cannot reconstruct from this dest; I verified the code path and the preconditions instead.

## Findings

### 1. The "link" option in Expected #1 is categorically refused by a shipped security control -- `blocks-the-design`

**Evidence (executed, not cited).** `assertDepositContained` (`packages/core/src/deposit/contain.ts`, #2305) anchors on `realpath(projectDir)` and rejects any component of the deposit path that is a symlink resolving outside the project tree. I built the exact proposed shape in a temp fixture -- `<worktree>/.deft/core` as a junction to `<primary>/.deft/core` -- and called it:

```text
LINK: created (junction) -> true
CONTAIN(link): REFUSED -> DepositContainmentError | deposit refused: ...\wt\.deft\core is a
  symlink escaping the project tree (resolves to ...\primary\.deft\core, outside ...)
CONTAIN(copy): ACCEPTED
```

**Failure mode.** A worktree whose deposit is a link passes doctor once and then hard-refuses the next `directive init` / refresh in that tree with `DEPOSIT_CONTAINMENT_REFUSED_EXIT_CODE = 2` -- a harder, less legible failure than the one being fixed, surfacing later and on a different command. The guard cannot distinguish "sibling worktree of the same repo" from "attacker-planted `.deft -> ../../evil`" without being taught a new trust rule; the containment check is deliberately path-shaped, not repo-identity-shaped.

**Disposition consequence.** The lean cannot bind Expected #1 as written. Either strike `link` and bind on copy, or bind an explicit #2305 amendment carrying its own threat re-argument. "Reuse, copy, or link" reads as three interchangeable options; one of them is refused by code that exists to refuse it.

### 2. Expected #3 names an advisory emitter, so satisfying it does not change the exit code -- `blocks-the-design`

**Evidence.** The quoted string is `plan().nextAction.rootCause` (`resolution/plan.ts:174`). `runResolutionDecision` files it at `severity: "warning"` (`doctor/main.ts:1861-1875`). Doctor's exit is `errorCount > 0 ? 1 : 0`, and `errorCount` counts only `severity: "error"` (`doctor/main.ts:711-713`). The errors in a deposit-less consumer tree come from deposit-dependent checks elsewhere -- e.g. `consumer-check-graph-integrity` files `severity: "error"` when the deposit root does not resolve `CONSUMER_CHECK_GATES` (`doctor/main.ts:1236-1249`), plus the structure and install-integrity checks that only run outside the framework repo.

**Failure mode.** A remedy that rewrites the resolution row's root cause, its next command, or adds a "linked worktree of a healthy primary" operating-mode string leaves `errorCount` untouched. `deft doctor` still exits 1, the gated `doctor` step still fails, and `session:ready` is exactly as blocked as before. The issue's "at minimum" floor would ship and deliver nothing.

**Disposition consequence.** If the lean keeps a minimum-viable tier, it must name the *error-emitting* checks as the remediation surface, not the resolution line. Otherwise strike the tier -- a floor that cannot move the gate is not a floor.

### 3. Expected #2 cannot fix the repro this issue filed -- `blocks-the-design`

**Evidence.** The issue's own Reproduction creates the tree "via the host's worktree tool". Framework-owned `git worktree add` callsites at the pin are `swarm/worktrees.ts:167`, `triage/evaluate/worktrees.ts:36`, and `design-critique/arc-dest.ts:184`. Swarm's C3 path explicitly *consumes* an operator-supplied worktree map instead of creating trees (`content/skills/deft-directive-swarm/references/core-phase-1-2.md:39`).

**Failure mode.** Provision-at-reserve covers none of: the interactive escape #4290 prescribes, a host worktree tool, or a C3 pre-created map. The reported defect, and the escape route the issue argues is mandatory, both survive a complete implementation of Expected #2.

**Disposition consequence.** The issue says "Any of these would fix the class." That is false for #2. The lean must either demote #2 to a complement of #1 or drop the any-of framing; binding #2 alone would close this issue without fixing the observation that opened it.

### 4. The deposit source should be the pinned content payload, not the sibling tree -- `sharpens-framing`

**Evidence.** `reconstituteDepositFromContent(contentRoot, deftDir, copyContent)` already exists (`init-deposit/gitignore.ts:439`) and copies from the resolved content root, not from another checkout; `contentRoot()` resolves `@deftai/directive-content` / source `content/` / vendored deposit (`packages/core/src/content-root.ts`). `untrack-core.ts:176` records the intended invariant: the committed pin is what "lets `directive update` reconstitute". Meanwhile `contentStale` compares `facts.deftCorePayloadVersion` against `facts.pinVersion` (`resolution/plan.ts:115-125`), and both are read from the *current* tree.

**Failure mode.** Copy-from-primary imports the primary's payload version into a tree whose committed pin may be ahead -- the ordinary case where the worktree's branch bumped `@deftai/directive`. The copy lands, `contentStale` trips, doctor routes to `update`, and the worktree still does not pass on the first try, which is the whole complaint.

**Disposition consequence.** Bind the source as the pinned content payload resolved locally (no network), with the common dir used for *detection* only and the sibling tree as a fallback. Stated that way, Expected #1 is mostly assembling primitives that already ship -- a much smaller bind than the issue's wording implies.

### 5. `.deft/` is not the deposit -- it is also per-tree lease and session state -- `sharpens-framing`

**Evidence.** The primary `.deft/` here holds `occupancy.json`, `authz/`, `child-occupancy/`, `session-binds/`, `spawn-reservations/`, `swarm-launch-occupancy/`, `ritual-state.json`, `last-session.json`, `cache/`. `occupancyPath` is `join(resolve(projectRoot), ".deft", "occupancy.json")` (`session/occupancy.ts:75,242`), and the code already carries the warning in prose at `occupancy.ts:249`: "Occupancy is per working tree. A copied `.deft/occupancy.json` from another checkout, image, or deposit still reads as a live foreign occupant". Sibling per-tree paths: `child-occupancy.ts:28`, `ritual-sentinel.ts:18-19`, `orientation-state.ts:12`, `spawn-occupancy.ts:766`.

**Failure mode.** The issue says "`.deft/` is gitignored" and then asks to "reuse, copy, or link the existing healthy deposit". Read at `.deft/` granularity -- which is how the sentence scans -- a copy transplants a live lease record into a new tree (the #3926 foreign-residue bug that comment was written to prevent), and a link makes every worktree read and write the primary's `occupancy.json`. That would evaluate the #4290 primary-checkout refusal against shared state -- the mechanism the issue invokes as its own motivation.

**Disposition consequence.** The Bound remedy must scope to `.deft/core/` in words, not leave "the deposit" to be resolved by the implementer. Cheap to state, expensive to get wrong.

### 6. Deposit presence is load-bearing as a repo-mode discriminator -- `sharpens-framing`

**Evidence.** `runningInsideDeftRepo` returns false the moment `.deft/core` exists (`doctor/paths.ts:157-173`, line 170). Doctor gates its Resolution section, install-integrity, managed-section freshness, hook registration, Taskfile-include and consumer-check-graph checks on that predicate (`doctor/main.ts:704, 972, 1069, 1142, 1210, 1265`). Verified live: `deft doctor` in this framework-repo linked worktree exits 0 with those checks skipped. Also verified: `C:\Repos\deft\directive\.deft\core` **does not exist** -- this repo's own primary checkout has no deposit, because it is a source checkout resolving through `content/`.

**Failure mode.** An unconditional reserve-time provisioner that deposits `.deft/core` into a framework-repo worktree flips that tree from maintainer to consumer classification and switches on consumer-only error checks inside a maintainer tree. And the copy-from-primary remedy has *no source* in this repo: the predicate "primary checkout holds a healthy deposit" is false here, on the very repo the framework is developed in.

**Disposition consequence.** The lean must state the no-healthy-primary branch explicitly, and it must not be "tell the operator to init the primary" -- that would deposit `.deft/core` into a source checkout and silently reclassify it. Name the fallback (pinned payload per finding 4, or leave the existing message) rather than letting it fall through.

### 7. Footnotes

- `footnote` -- The extraction rationale in "Relationship to existing issues" is stale. #4409 has since been recut; its body now reads "Deposit reconstitution stays on #4443" and "Do not close that issue from this recut" under an accepted synthesis. The risk the extraction hedged against ("may be resolved on the identity axis without touching this") is already closed by #4409's own bound remedy. No disposition weight; the extraction was still the right call.
- `footnote` -- Protocol observation, no disposition weight on #4443. The contract fixes the round-1 ceiling at the triage write-back, and separately requires a `role: parent` panel-deposit before the first sibling spawn for N>=3. Those two rules put the deposit strictly above every sibling's ceiling by construction, so no sibling can verify panel completeness from inside its envelope. I am not asserting a missing deposit -- I cannot see one either way, and I have not read past 5650304466.

## Injection / swarm lens

Triggered: the target changes occupancy, worktrees, and shared state. Not collapsed into identity.

- **Worktrees.** Findings 1, 3, 6. The deposit path is exactly the surface #2305 hardened, and worktree provenance is not a trust signal the containment guard accepts.
- **Occupancy.** Finding 5. The blast radius of getting the granularity wrong is lease correctness across every spawned worker, not a slow first turn.
- **Identity.** Clean here, and should stay clean: #4409's recut split owner derivation onto its own number. Nothing in Expected #1-#3 needs to read or mint an owner, and the lean should say so rather than leaving room for a provisioner to also stamp identity into the new tree.
- **Untrusted input.** A copy-from-primary remedy reads bytes from a path derived from `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`. Influencing that output requires write access to `.git`, which is already terminal, so this is not a new surface. The real exposure is finding 1: `.deft` path components are attacker-shaped, which is why the guard exists.

## Road not taken

I considered recommending that doctor gain a fourth operating mode ("linked worktree of a healthy primary") as the primary remedy, since `runningInsideDeftRepo` is the precedent and the seam already exists. I rejected it on finding 2: the operating-mode line is display, and the checks that fail are elsewhere. A new mode string would read like progress and move nothing.

## Steelman of the strongest rejected position

The strongest case against findings 1 and 2 is that they are implementation detail: the issue says "any of these would fix the class", so an implementer would discover that the link is refused and that the warning is not the error, and route around both. I reject that on the contract's own terms -- closing a finding with "a reviewer would catch it" is a failed finding -- and on a specific one: Expected #3 is written as the *minimum acceptable* outcome, so it is the tier most likely to be bound under time pressure, and it is the tier that provably cannot move the gate.

**What would flip finding 1.** Evidence that `assertDepositContained` is not on the path a worktree deposit would take -- a provisioning route that never calls the contained deposit code. I did not find one; every reconstitution route at the pin funnels through it.

**What would flip finding 2.** A consumer-repo `deft doctor --json` capture from the reported session showing `severity: "error"` on `check: "resolution"`. That would mean the resolution finding's severity is conditional in a way I did not read. I could not reproduce a consumer tree from this dest.

The payload-absence half stands on a consumer tree. The gitignore / "full init" / "link the deposit" half does not. The recorded target can bind only after those three are scoped.

## Existing mechanisms (inventory first)

- `git worktree add` copies tracked files only. Live: `git worktree add --detach` at this SHA produced `.deft/` (tracked `.deft/approved-scope/*`) and no `.deft/core`, no `.deft/occupancy.json`, no `node_modules`.

- Consumer gitignore is not that blanket. `CANONICAL_GITIGNORE_BASELINE` ignores `.deft/core/`, `.deft/.cli/`, `.deft/occupancy.json`, `.deft/ritual-state.json` as separate lines. Occupancy and ritual are already per-tree by that split.

## 1. Link or whole-.deft reuse cannot be an equivalent remedy
blocks-the-design

Evidence: deposit containment refuses an escaping `.deft/core` symlink. Occupancy and ritual live under `.deft/` next to the payload and are gitignored separately on consumers. A shared `.deft` (symlink or junction of the directory) is one occupancy file; claim-over on the worktree would rewrite the primary lease. Byte-copy of the whole directory still plants the primary's `occupancy.json` and `ritual-state.json` (mitigated only after path mismatch is noticed).

Failure mode: bind accepts "reuse, copy, or link the existing healthy deposit" as equivalent. Implementers link `.deft/core` → doctor/update throw containment. Or they link/copy `.deft/` → two trees share or clobber identity. The occupancy isolation that forced the worktree escape is undone.

Disposition: the lean cannot bind while "link" or whole-`.deft` copy remains an accepted equivalent. Accepted reuse is payload-only: copy `.deft/core` bytes, or call existing `directive update` reconstitution. Occupancy, ritual, authz, and dest-lock stay per-tree.

## 2. Doctor's printed ladder is init; the missing bytes are already update-shaped
sharpens-framing

Evidence: live consumer doctor next command is `npx @deftai/directive init`. `updateStateFromPlan` maps managed-section + missing payload to `updated`. Refresh copies the content package into `.deft/core` from the running CLI, so a worktree without `node_modules` can still reconstitute if the engine is on PATH. Full init also scaffolds gitignore, hooks, and xbrief that `git worktree add` already copied as tracked files.

Failure mode: bind keeps "until a full directive init" as the required repair. Every worktree pays network/onboarding, then discards it on `git worktree remove`. Doctor keeps pointing at the heavy verb while the light one already materializes the payload.

Disposition: bind can proceed if the local remediation is `directive update` (or an equivalent payload copy) that `session:ready` runs, not a per-worktree `directive init`.

## 3. session:ready claims the tree, then doctor fails closed
sharpens-framing

Evidence: `session:ready` order is occupancy claim then gated doctor. Consumer doctor exit 1 is install-integrity, so the ritual doctor step fails after the lease exists. Primary mutation claim is already refuse, so the sanctioned escape is this tree.

Failure mode: first `session:ready` in a fresh worktree always burns a lease on a tree that cannot pass doctor. A later ready is then a presentation/lease problem, not a deposit problem. Expected-3 "doctor names a distinct state" without ready running the remediation leaves that order in place.

Disposition: bind only if reconstitution runs in the same `session:ready` that would otherwise claim-then-fail, before doctor is the gated stop. Doctor-text alone is not the fix.

## 4. Framework worktree provision does not cover the filed path
sharpens-framing

Evidence: swarm `createWorktree` and dest-lock persist do not copy `.deft/core`. The filed reproduction is a host worktree tool (`git worktree add` / Claude worktree), not swarm Phase 2. `mainWorktreeRoot` already knows the primary; nothing consumes it for payload.

Failure mode: bind takes Expected 2 (provision on framework worktree create) as sufficient. Host-native linked worktrees stay born without a payload. Swarm workers and interactive escapes stay split.

Disposition: Expected 2 may complement. The host-agnostic gate is session/doctor reconstitution on any linked worktree whose common-dir primary already has a healthy `.deft/core`. Do not collapse this extract into a Grok-dispatch identity leak.

## Injection / swarm lens

Triggered: identity, occupancy, worktrees, shared state. This is the host-agnostic worktree+payload hole, not a Grok-identity defect.

- Identity: occupancy is a cooperative bearer-id on `.deft/occupancy.json` per working tree. Sharing that file across primary and dest merges two actors.
- Occupancy: primary claim is refuse; dest-place reserves a linked worktree then claims. Reservation does not plant a payload, so the dest is occupiable and doctor-red.
- Worktrees: common-dir is already the dest-lock and main-root locator. Use it to find the primary payload. Do not use it to share occupancy, ritual, or authz.

A reviewer would not be the control. Deterministic control is: payload materialization that cannot write occupancy/ritual, plus containment that already refuses escaping deposit links.

## Road not taken

Chose payload-only reconstitution (existing `directive update`, or copy of `.deft/core` bytes from `mainWorktreeRoot`). Rejected symlink/junction (containment + occupancy merge). Rejected swarm-only provision as the sole fix (misses host-native add).

Steelmans of copy-from-primary: no content-package resolve, works fully offline, matches "primary already healthy." What would flip: `session:ready` calls `directive update` via the running CLI, doctor goes green, occupancy file is never copied. Then primary-copy is a shortcut, not the contract.
